record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: Are large-field natural-inflation models built from one or more axions compatible with a ultraviolet-complete theory of quantum gravity, either because an explicit string-theory construction exists or because a strict no-go theorem proves that no such construction is possible?

evidence.quote: Determining whether or not such models are compatible with quantum gravity, either through an explicit example in string theory or a strict no-go theorem, remains a significant open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A natural-inflation model is an inflationary cosmological model in which the inflaton is one or several pseudo-scalar axion fields φ_i (i = 1, …, N), each enjoying a discrete shift symmetry φ_i → φ_i + 2π f_i with axion decay constants f_i, and whose potential is generated by non-perturbative (instanton) effects, taking the schematic form

  V(φ) = Σ_k Λ_k^4 [1 − cos(Σ_i n_{k,i} φ_i / f_i + δ_k)],

with integer charges n_{k,i}, dynamical scales Λ_k, and phases δ_k. Such a model is called "large-field" if successful slow-roll inflation requires the inflaton to traverse a field range Δφ that is parametrically super-Planckian, i.e. Δφ ≳ M_Pl (equivalently, at least one effective decay constant satisfies f_eff ≳ M_Pl).

The question: Determine whether large-field natural-inflation models, built from one or several axions in the above sense, can be ultraviolet-completed in a consistent theory of quantum gravity. Specifically, establish one of the following:

(a) an explicit construction within string theory (or another known consistent quantum-gravity framework) of a four-dimensional effective theory realizing large-field natural inflation with parametrically controlled super-Planckian axion field range and a potential of the form above; or

(b) a strict no-go theorem proving that no such ultraviolet completion exists, i.e. that any effective field theory admitting a consistent embedding in quantum gravity necessarily fails to satisfy the conditions defining large-field natural inflation.
artifact.category_tag: axion inflation and quantum gravity swampland
artifact.status_search_result: The compatibility of large-field natural inflation with quantum gravity remains an active and unresolved area. Swampland and weak-gravity-conjecture arguments give partial obstructions (e.g., single closed-string axion models conflict with the WGC, and simple 2-axion aligned-winding models fail by a no-go theorem), but these can sometimes be evaded with multiple axions or alignment among three or more axions. No explicit, parametrically controlled string-theory construction nor a strict universal no-go theorem has been established.

status_evidence.title: Fencing in the swampland: quantum gravity constraints on large field inflation
status_evidence.snippet: Obstacles to large-field inflation in string theory are traced to swampland conjectures; parametrically controllable large single-field inflation appears impossible in string theory if these conjectures hold.
status_evidence.claim: Strong but conjectural obstructions, not a proof.

status_evidence.title: Large field ranges from aligned and misaligned winding
status_evidence.snippet: Two-axion aligned winding fails by a general no-go theorem, but the obstruction is avoided by aligning three or more axions, yielding large decay constants.
status_evidence.claim: Partial no-go theorems exist with known evasions, indicating the general question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Constraints on axion inflation from the weak gravity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Single closed-string-axion natural inflation incompatible with WGC.
status_evidence.claim: Particular classes are constrained, but the general statement remains open.

status_evidence.title: Production of gravitational waves by inflationary transitions in aligned natural inflation (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Continued investigation of aligned natural-inflation constructions in 2025.
